messages:
Carlos: Hey team — since 2026-03-12 04:10 UTC we've seen intermittent failures from our service when calling Redwood's /v1/sign. Errors look like `KMSError: KeyNotAvailable` and `HSM_CONN_RESET`. Affected region: us-east-1, cluster: ch-cluster-7. Roughly 1 in 20 sign requests fail. Payment processing is impacted. Audit logs for 04:10-04:25 show missing entries for those requests. Can you triage?

Amelia (support): Thanks Carlos — sorry to hear that. I'm escalating to SRE and Security. @Samir @Jing please take a look. Carlos, can you paste a minimal repro curl + one example request ID and the HSM cluster id? Also confirm whether this key was rotated recently.

Carlos: Sample repro (prod credentials redacted):
```
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/sign \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"key_id":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234","digest":"..."}' \
    || echo "FAIL $i";
done
```
One failing request from logs: request_id=req_20260312_0413_789, timestamp=2026-03-12T04:13:22Z, error="KMSError: KeyNotAvailable", hsm_node=hsm-07. Cluster id: ch-cluster-7. Key was rotated last week during maintenance window.

Samir (sre): Got it. A few quick asks and a controlled repro:
1) Can you run the above loop but with `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug` and capture 500 calls, include the raw HSM response snippets.
2) Provide the HSM serials you see (you provided hsm-07; any others reporting errors?).
3) Run the cloudhsm health check: `aws cloudhsmv2 describe-clusters --cluster-ids ch-cluster-7` and share the `state` and `clusterCertificates` field.
4) If possible, do a single-threaded 200-call run to see if failures correlate to concurrency.

Also note: missing audit entries suggests our audit forwarder didn't ingest some events or the KMS->HSM proxy returned before logging. @Jing will look at ingestion.

Jing (security): This is high priority for compliance. Missing audit events during a payments window is a finding if we can't produce logs. Please:
- Preserve all raw logs from 2026-03-12 04:00 to 04:30 UTC (don't rotate/compress).
- Share any CloudTrail entries for the KMS/key usage in that window.
- If you rotated keys last week, provide the rotation runbook/trace and which key version the service is using now.

Amelia (support): I've created internal incident IR-2026-045 and tagged SRE + Security. OpsBot — create incident IR-2026-045.

OpsBot: Incident IR-2026-045 created (priority: P1). Notifying oncall.

Carlos: Ran the requested tests. Results: out of 500 sequential sign calls (single-threaded) we got 17 failures. Failures clustered to node hsm-07 and timestamps mostly between 04:12:30-04:14:10 UTC. Sample raw HSM fragment: `ERR: HSM_CONN_RESET during sign, socket errno=104, seq=324`. CloudHSM describe-clusters shows cluster state ACTIVE, 3 HSMs: hsm-05, hsm-06, hsm-07. hsm-07 reported higher packet loss in our monitoring for that window.

Samir (sre): That points to node-level networking flakiness between our KMS bridge and hsm-07. Two immediate actions:
- Short term: Add automatic retry with jitter for sign calls that receive HSM_CONN_RESET (we already have a 2x retry; propose 5 retries with exponential backoff for P1 payment paths).
- Triage: collect tcpdump on the bridge host for 04:12-04:15 and enable HSM agent debug logs. Example tcpdump command: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/hsm-bridge-0412.pcap host <hsm-07-ip> and port 2224`.

Also run this repro from our bridge host (not from app host) to isolate network: `seq 1 500 | xargs -n1 -P1 -I{} curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/sign -d '{"key_id":"<key>","digest":"..."}'` and attach bridge logs.

Jing (security): For audit/compliance: we need to ensure the missing log events are recovered or we document the gap with root cause. Please export the raw audit buffer if possible (`/var/log/redwood/audit-buffer.log`) and stop log rotation as Samir said. If any messages were dropped in the forwarder due to transient HSM errors, capture the forwarder metrics (`forwarder.dropped_events`).

Carlos: Attached results (pasted small excerpt):
```
2026-03-12T04:12:34Z req_... OK
2026-03-12T04:12:35Z req_... HSM_CONN_RESET (hsm-07)
2026-03-12T04:12:36Z req_... OK
2026-03-12T04:12:38Z req_... HSM_CONN_RESET (hsm-07)
```
I confirmed forwarder.dropped_events spiked to 23 at 04:14 UTC.

Samir (sre): Good find. Likely sequence: HSM node flapped -> bridge observed socket resets -> KMS proxy dropped/returned error before audit forwarder persisted event -> customer sees sign failures and missing audit rows. Next steps:
- I'll open a support case with AWS CloudHSM with cluster id ch-cluster-7 and attach pcap + HSM agent logs. (Samir -> AWS case # will be posted)
- Apply the retry bump for payment route as a hotfix (Amelia: can you approve emergency config change?).
- Coordinate a rolling reboot of hsm-07 during a controlled maintenance window if AWS confirms node-level issue.

Amelia (support): Approving retry bump for the payment route now and scheduling a 30-min maintenance window tonight 02:00-02:30 UTC to allow for possible HSM reboot (pending AWS confirmation). Meanwhile Jing, please document the audit gap with the initial findings for compliance.

Jing (security): I'll draft the compliance entry and request evidence retention. Also asking legal for notification requirements if any customer data exposures are found.

Carlos: Thanks all — appreciate the rapid response. I'll keep capturing logs and will add the pcap + bridge logs to the incident. Please keep me posted on AWS support case number and the planned maintenance.

Samir (sre): Will post AWS case # and ETA here. For now please do not rotate or rekey — preserves evidence.

Amelia (support): We'll follow up in the incident thread IR-2026-045. :thumbsup:
